U867.5 Jump to heading ¶

Abán son of Cinaed, heir designate of Connacht, was killed with fire by Sochlachán son of Diarmait.

U867.6 Jump to heading ¶

Auisle, one of three kings of the heathens, was killed by his kinsmen in guile and parricide.

U867.7 Jump to heading ¶

The dark foreigners won a battle over the northern Saxons at York, in which fell Aelle, king of the northern Saxons.

U867.8 Jump to heading ¶

Amlaíb's fort at Cluain Dolcáin was burned by Gaíthíne's son and Mael Ciaráin son of Rónán, and the aforesaid commanders caused a slaughter of a hundred of the leaders of the foreigners in the vicinity of Cluain Dolcáin on the same day.

U867.9 Jump to heading ¶

Muiredach son of Cathal, king of Uí Chremthainn, died of prolonged paralysis.

U868.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 867.

U868.1 Jump to heading ¶

Cellach son of Cumuscach, abbot of Fobar, a learned and most talented young man, died.

U868.2 Jump to heading ¶

Connmach, abbot of Cluain Moccu Nóis, fell asleep in Christ on the night of the Kalends 1st of January.

U868.3 Jump to heading ¶

Daniél, abbot of Glenn dá Locha and Tamlacht, and Caemán son of Dálach, abbot of Dam Liac, died.

U868.4 Jump to heading ¶

Aed son of Niall won a battle at Cell Ua nDaigri against the Uí Néill of Brega, and the Laigin, and a large force of the foreigners, i.e. three hundred or more; and Flann son of Conaing, king of all Brega, and Diarmait son of Etarscéle, king of Loch Gabor, fell therein; and in this battle very many of the heathens were slaughtered; and

p.325

Fachtna son of Mael Dúin, heir designate of the North, and many others, fell in the counter-attack of the battle.

  1. (Flann son of Conaing, a king until now,

Took the land once held by Tadc son of Cian;

He was a golden shoot to protect the seed of Niall

That had sprouted from the fairy hill of good Cerna. 2. It is strange to look at the estuary of the Boyne

(It is fitting to keep a pact in mind)

And not to see the active(?) warrior of Fernach(?)

Flann of populous Bregmag.)

U868.5 Jump to heading ¶

Congal son of Fedach, abbot of Cell Delga, a scribe, rested.

U868.6 Jump to heading ¶

A remarkable eruption of water from Sliab Cualann, with little black fishes.

U868.7 Jump to heading ¶

A great windstorm on the Feast of Martin 11 Nov.

U868.8 Jump to heading ¶

Rechtabra son of Murchad, abbot of Corcach Mór, fell asleep.

U869.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 868.

U869.1 Jump to heading ¶

Martan, abbot of Cluain Moccu Nóis and Daiminis, a scribe, and Niallán, bishop of Sláine, fell asleep.

U869.2 Jump to heading ¶

Cormac son of Éládach, abbot of Saiger, bishop and scribe, ended his life as a very old man.

U869.3 Jump to heading ¶

Flann son of Ferchar, steward of Ard Macha and superior of Lann Léire, ended alas! a short life.

U869.4 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Ciaráin son of Rónán, royal champion of eastern Ireland, a warrior who plundered the foreigners, was killed.

U869.5 Jump to heading ¶

Cernach son of Eochu, chief of Mugdorna of Brega, and Ruadachán son of Niall, chief of Uí Fhorannán, died.

U869.6 Jump to heading ¶

Ard Macha was plundered by Amlaíb and burned with its oratories. Ten hundred were carried off or killed, and great rapine also committed.

U869.7 Jump to heading ¶

Donnacán son of Cétfaid, king of Uí Cheinnselaig, was treacherously killed by his companion.

U869.8 Jump to heading ¶

Ailill of Clochar, scribe, bishop and abbot of Clochar Mac nDaiméni, fell asleep.

U869.9 Jump to heading ¶

Dubthach son of Mael Tuile, most learned of the Latinists of all Europe, fell asleep in Christ.

U869.10 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Brigte son of Spelán, king of Conaille, died in clerical life.

p.327

U870.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 869.

U870.1 Jump to heading ¶

Suairlech of Int Eidnén, bishop and anchorite and abbot of Cluain Iraird, the best exponent of religion in all Ireland, rested.

U870.2 Jump to heading ¶

Aed son of Niall overran Laigin from Áth Cliath to Gabruán. Cerball son of Dúngal with what force he could gather invaded them and reached Dún Bolg. The Laigin attacked Cerball's encampment and slew Gaíthíne's son and others, and were then thrown back in flight with their king i.e. Muiredach son of Bran, and some of them were slaughtered.

U870.3 Jump to heading ¶

Dálach son of Muirchertach, chief of Cenél Conaill, was killed by his own people.

U870.4 Jump to heading ¶

Diarmait son of Diarmait killed a man in Ard Macha in front of the door of the house of Aed, king of Temair.

U870.5 Jump to heading ¶

Dub dá Thuile, abbot of Liath Mór Mo-Chaemóc, and the anchorite Maelodar, abbot of Daiminis, and the abbot of Ciarán's hermitage of Belach Dúin, i.e. Cumscuth, a scribe and a bishop; Comgán the Tall, anchorite of Tamlacht and disciple of Mael Ruain; Connla, anchorite of Druim Cara of Ard Ciannacht—all ended their lives in Christ.

U870.6 Jump to heading ¶

The siege of Ail Cluaithe by the Norsemen: Amlaíb and Ímar, two kings of the Norsemen, laid siege to the fortress and at the end of four months they destroyed and plundered it.

U870.7 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Sechnaill son of Niall, one of the two kings of southern Brega, was treacherously killed by Ulf the dark foreigner.

U870.8 Jump to heading ¶

Cobthach son of Muiredach, superior of Cell Dara, fell asleep.

U871.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 870.

U871.1 Jump to heading ¶

Cathalán son of Indrechtach, one of two kings of Ulaid, was deceitfully killed at the instigation of Aed.

U871.2 Jump to heading ¶

Amlaíb and Ímar returned to Áth Cliath from Alba with two hundred ships, bringing away with them in captivity to Ireland a great prey of Angles and Britons and Picts.

U871.3 Jump to heading ¶

The storming of Dún Sobairche, which had never been achieved before: the foreigners were at it with the Cenél Eógain.

U871.4 Jump to heading ¶

Ailill son of Dúnlang, king of Laigin, was killed by the Norsemen.

p.329

U871.5 Jump to heading ¶

Bishop Ailill, abbot of Fobar, fell asleep in Christ.

U871.6 Jump to heading ¶

Cú Raí son of Aldnia, of Inis Clothrann and of Fochla of Mide, a learned abbot and the most expert in the histories of the Irish, fell asleep in Christ.

U871.7 Jump to heading ¶

Colgu son of Mael Tuile, priest, anchorite and abbot of Cluain Chonaire Tómáin, rested.

U871.8 Jump to heading ¶

The pilgrim Maengal, abbot of Bennchor, happily ended his life as an old man.

U871.9 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Mide son of Cumuscach, prior of Cluain Moccu Nóis, dies.

U872.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 871.

U872.1 Jump to heading ¶

Gnia, superior of Dam Liac, an anchorite, bishop and excellent scribe, died.

U872.2 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Ruanaid, son of Mael Curarda, chief of Uí Moccu Uais of the North, died.

U872.3 Jump to heading ¶

Cenn Faelad grandson of Mochtigern, king of Caisel, rested in peace after prolonged suffering.

U872.4 Jump to heading ¶

Ferdomnach, superior of Cluain Moccu Nóis, fell asleep.

U872.5 Jump to heading ¶

Artgal, king of the Britons of Strathclyde, was killed at the instigation of Constantine son of Cinaed.

U872.6 Jump to heading ¶

Bishop Mael Tuile, superior of Tuilén, fell asleep in Christ.

U872.7 Jump to heading ¶

Loingsech son of Foillén, superior of Cell Ausile, dies.

U872.8 Jump to heading ¶

Robartach of Dairmag, an excellent scribe, rested.

U872.9 Jump to heading ¶

Mugrón son of Mael Cothaid, one of two kings of Connacht, died.

U873.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January twenty-seventh of the moon. AD 872.

U873.1 Jump to heading ¶

Flaithbertach son of Dub Roip, king of Corcu Mruad Ninais, Uathmarán son of Brócán, king of Uí Fhiachrach Aidni, and Dúnadach son of Rogallach, king of Cenél Cairpri Móir, die.

U873.2 Jump to heading ¶

Lethlabar son of Loingsech, king of the Province, ended his life as an old man.

U873.3 Jump to heading ¶

Ímar, king of the Norsemen of all Ireland and Britain, ended his life.

U873.4 Jump to heading ¶

Dúngal son of Maenach, superior of Inis Caín Dega, rested in peace.

p.331

U873.5 Jump to heading ¶

Donn Cuan son of Flannacán, was treacherously killed by Conaing son of Flann.

U873.6 Jump to heading ¶

The fair of Tailtiu was not held, although there was no just and worthy reason for this—something which we have not known to happen from ancient times.

U873.7 Jump to heading ¶

Colmán, bishop, scribe and abbot of Naendruim, rested.

U873.8 Jump to heading ¶

Flaithbertach son of Muirchertach, superior of Dún Caillen, died.

U874.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January ninth of the moon
[...]
.AD 873.

U874.1 Jump to heading ¶

Aed son of Fiangus, superior of Ros Comáin, a bishop and an excellent scribe, and Mael Mórda son of Diarmait, a bishop and scribe, died.

U874.2 Jump to heading ¶

Torpaid, superior of Tamlacht, a bishop and excellent scribe, fell asleep in Christ.

U874.3 Jump to heading ¶

Bishop Féthgna, successor of Patrick and head of religion in all Ireland, rested in peace on the day before the Nones 6th of October.

U874.4 Jump to heading ¶

Aed son of Niall led an army to Laigin and they profaned Cell Ausili, and other churches were burned with their oratories.

U874.5 Jump to heading ¶

Cell Mór of Mag Enir was plundered by the foreigners.

U875.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January twentieth of the moon
[...]
. AD 874.

U875.1 Jump to heading ¶

Maengal, tanist of Cluain Moccu Nóis, and Robartach son of the Artificer, bishop of Cell Dara and an excellent scribe and the superior of Cell Achaid, and Lachtnán son of Mochtigern, bishop of Cell Dara and superior of Ferna, died.

U875.2 Jump to heading ¶

Muiredach son of Bran, with the army of the Laigin, laid waste the country as far as Sliab Monduirn and returned to his own territory before evening.

U875.3 Jump to heading ¶

The Picts encountered the dark foreigners in battle, and a great slaughter of the Picts resulted.

U875.4 Jump to heading ¶

Oistín son of Amlaíb, king of the Norsemen, was deceitfully killed by Albann.

U875.5 Jump to heading ¶

Mac Oige, superior of Tamlacht, and Mael Bennachta, bishop of Lusca, fell asleep in peace.

U875.6 Jump to heading ¶

Fechtnach, abbot of Glenn dá Locha, died.

U876.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January first of the moon
[...]
. AD 875.

U876.1 Jump to heading ¶

Constantine son of Cinaed, king of the Picts, Cinaed

p.333

abbot of Achad Bó Cainnig, Congalach son of Fínnechta, king of the Airgialla, and Fedach, superior of Dísert Diarmata, die.

U876.2 Jump to heading ¶

Cairpre son of Diarmait, king of Uí Cheinnselaig, was killed by his own kinsmen.

U876.3 Jump to heading ¶

The fair of Tailtiu was not held, although there was no just and worthy reason for this.

U876.4 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall, bishop of Corcach, an excellent scribe, died suddenly.

U877.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January twelfth of the moon
[...]
. AD 876.

U877.1 Jump to heading ¶

Eógan and Mael Tuile, grandson of Cuanu, two abbots of Cluain Moccu Nóis, fell asleep in peace.

U877.2 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad son of Aedacán son of Conchobor, was deceitfully killed by Flann son of Mael Sechnaill.

U877.3 Jump to heading ¶

Rhodri son of Merfyn, king of the Britons, came in flight from the dark foreigners to Ireland.

U877.4 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Brigte, bishop of Sláine, fell asleep in peace.

U877.5 Jump to heading ¶

A skirmish at Loch Cuan between the fair heathens and the dark heathens, in which Albann, king of the dark heathens, fell.

U877.6 Jump to heading ¶

Sochartach son of Brócán, chief of Uí Chormaic, died.

U877.7 Jump to heading ¶

A change of abbots in Ard Macha, i.e. Ainmire instead of Mael Coba.

U877.8 Jump to heading ¶

Cathalán son of Cernach, king of Fir Chúl, dies.

U878.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January twenty-third of the moon
[...]
. AD 877.

U878.1 Jump to heading ¶

Rhodri son of Merfyn, king of the Britons, was killed by the Saxons.

U878.2 Jump to heading ¶

Aed son of Cinaed, king of the Picts, was killed by his own associates.

U878.3 Jump to heading ¶

Gairbíth son of Mael Brigte, king of Conaille, was beheaded by the Uí Echach.

  1. (Rhodri of Manu, splendid here,

Aed from the lands of Cenn Tíre,

Donnchad, lustrous stuff of sovereignty,

Gairíth, diadem of smooth Macha— 2. Whenever I bring it to mind

It inflames the limits of my heart,

Cold flags over temples of the buried,

Barrfhinn of Bile is distraught.)

p.335

U878.4 Jump to heading ¶

Cumuscach son of Muiredach, king of Uí Chremthainn, was killed by the Ulaid.

U878.5 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Pátraic son of Cellach, superior of Mainister Buiti, died suddenly.

U878.6 Jump to heading ¶

Great wind and lightning. A shower of blood fell and clots of gore and blood were found in the fields.

U878.7 Jump to heading ¶

The fair of Tailtiu was not held, although there was no just and worthy reason for this.

U878.8 Jump to heading ¶

There was a lunar eclipse on the Ides 15th of October, the fourteenth of the moon, on the fourth feria about the third watch; and a solar eclipse on the fourth of the Kalends of November 29 October, the twenty-eighth of the moon, on the fourth feria, about the seventh hour of daylight, fifteen solar days having intervened.

U878.9 Jump to heading ¶

The shrine of Colum Cille and his other halidoms arrived in Ireland, having been taken in flight to escape the foreigners.

U879.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January fourth of the moon
[...]
. AD 878.

U879.1 Jump to heading ¶

Aed son of Niall, king of Temair, fell asleep on the twelfth of the Kalends of December 20 Nov. at Druim Inasclainn in the territory of Conaille.

  1. (Twelve days before the melodious Kalends

Of December—a harsh company—

A wonderful person died to your loss(?),

Aed of Ailech, over-king of the Irish. 2. A generous prudent man of shields

Who brought plenty to landed Temair,

Against iron-tipped spears a buckler

From the forge-fire of the land of the sons of Mil.)

U879.2 Jump to heading ¶

(Flann son of Mael Sechnaill begins to reign.)

U879.3 Jump to heading ¶

Bishop Tigernach son of Muiredach, superior of Druim Inasclainn, rested after prolonged suffering.

U879.4 Jump to heading ¶

Fergil son of Cumsad, abbot of Domnach Sechnaill, was secretly murdered.

U879.5 Jump to heading ¶

Aengus son of Cinaed, chief of the people of Ard Ciannachta, dies.

U879.6 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Coba son of Crunnmael, superior of Ard Macha, and the lector i.e. Mochta, were taken prisoner by the foreigners.

U879.7 Jump to heading ¶

Great scarcity of food for cattle in the spring. Great profusion in the autumn.

p.337

U879.8 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Caere, chief of Uí Chremthainn, was killed.

U879.9 Jump to heading ¶

Ualgarg son of Flaithbertach, heir designate of the North, dies.

U879.10 Jump to heading ¶

Finnechta son of Mael Corcra, king of the Luigni of Connacht, dies.

U879.11 Jump to heading ¶

Ainmire, superior of Ard Macha for nine months, fell asleep.

U879.12 Jump to heading ¶

Dúngal, superior of Lethglenn, dies.

U880.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January fifteenth of the moon
[...]
. AD. 879.

U880.1 Jump to heading ¶

Feradach son of Cormac, abbot of Í, rested.

U880.2 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Ciaráin son of Conaing, king of Tethba, ended his life as an old man in religion.

U880.3 Jump to heading ¶

Duiblitir, superior of Cluain Eóis and Tech Airennáin, died.

U880.4 Jump to heading ¶

Muirecán son of Cormaic, superior of Sentrabh, dies.

U880.5 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Mithig, son of Dub Indrecht, was killed.

U881.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January sixth of the moon
[...]
. AD 880.

U881.1 Jump to heading ¶

Ferchar, abbot of Bennchor, died.

U881.2 Jump to heading ¶

Crunnmael of Cluain Chaín, a bishop and anchorite, fell asleep.

U881.3 Jump to heading ¶

The oratory of Cianán was destroyed by the foreigners, and many people were taken from it. Afterwards Barith, a great despot of the Norsemen, was killed by St. Ciannán.

U881.4 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Sinchill son of Mugrón, king of Uí Fhailgi, dies.

U881.5 Jump to heading ¶

Aengus son of Mael Curarda, superior of Ard Sratha, Aenacán son of Ruaidrí, superior of Lusca, and Flaithemán son of Cellach, king of Uí Briúin of Cualu, die.

U881.6 Jump to heading ¶

Suibne, bishop of Cell Dara, rested.

U881.7 Jump to heading ¶

Bishop Ruidgel, abbot of Imlech Ibuir, rested.

U881.8 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Fábaill son of Loingsech, king of Carraic Brachaide, dies.

U882.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January seventh of the moon
[...]
. AD 881.

U882.1 Jump to heading ¶

Flann son of Mael Sechnaill led an army both of foreigners and Irish into the North. He camped at Mag eter dí Glais, and Ard Macha was invaded by him.

U882.2 Jump to heading ¶

Muirchertach son of Niall, abbot of Daire Calgaig, and other monasteries, rested.

p.339

U882.3 Jump to heading ¶

Lorcán son of Coscrach, king of Uí Nialláin, and Donnacán son of Fogartach, king of Fernmag, fell by one another.

U882.4 Jump to heading ¶

A skirmish between the Conaille of Muirtheimne and the Maid, in which fell Ainfíth son of Aed king of Ulaid, and Conallán son of Mael Dúin, king of Cuib, and other nobles. The Conaille were victors.

U882.5 Jump to heading ¶

Scannlán, superior of Dún Lethglaisi, was killed by the Ulaid.

U882.6 Jump to heading ¶

Cormac son of Ciarán, prior of Cluain Ferta Brénainn and superior of Tuaim dá Gualann, dies.

U882.7 Jump to heading ¶

Conchobor son of Tadc, king of the three Connachta, ended his life as an old man.

U882.8 Jump to heading ¶

Aedán, superior of Cluain Iraird, rested in peace.

U882.9 Jump to heading ¶

Dub Inse, superior of Inis Caín Dega, dies.

U883.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January eighteenth of the moon. AD 882.

U883.1 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Ruáin, bishop of Lusca, fell asleep in peace.

U883.2 Jump to heading ¶

Cumuscach son of Domnall, king of Cenél Loegaire, dies.

U883.3 Jump to heading ¶

Braen son of Tigernach was killed by Ainfíth son of Gairbíth.

  1. (Braen son of Tigernach the guileless

Who had a fine reputation in this world,

That Aengus should be slain like Braen(?),

Is it not one of the afflictions of God?)

U883.4 Jump to heading ¶

Death of Auisle's son at the hands of Iergne's son and the daughter of Mael Sechnaill.

U883.5 Jump to heading ¶

Ainfíth son of Mugrón, king of the Mugdorna of Brega, was killed.

U883.6 Jump to heading ¶

Eochucán son of Aed, one of two kings of Ulaid, was killed by the sons of Ainfíth son of Aed.

U883.7 Jump to heading ¶

Cathasach son of Robartach, superior of Ard Macha, rested in peace.

U883.8 Jump to heading ¶

Aengus son of Mael Dúin, heir designate of the North, was beheaded by the Dál Araidi.

p.341

U884.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January twenty-ninth of the moon
[...]
.AD 883.

U884.1 Jump to heading ¶

Ailbrenn son of Maicthech, superior of Cluain Iraird, fell asleep after a prolonged illness.

U884.2 Jump to heading ¶

Suairlech, superior of Ard Brecáin, ended his life as an old man.

U884.3 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall son of Muirecán, king of Laigin, was killed by his associates.

U884.4 Jump to heading ¶

Cairpre son of Dúnlang, king of western Life, died.

U884.5 Jump to heading ¶

Conaing son of Flann, heir designate of Cianacht, was beheaded by the Laigin.

U884.6 Jump to heading ¶

Donn Cuan son of Condálach, king of Cianacht of Glenn Geimin, dies.

U884.7 Jump to heading ¶

Dúnacán son of Tuathchar, king of Gailenga of Collumair, was killed by the Gailenga Móra.

U884.8 Jump to heading ¶

Cormac son of Ceithernach, prior of Tír dá Glas and Cluain Ferta Brénainn, rested.

U884.9 Jump to heading ¶

Rogaillnech, abbot of Bennchor, Dúnacán son of Cormac, abbot of Mainister Buiti, and Conallán son of Mael Teimin, superior of Inis Caín Dega, fell asleep.

U885.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January tenth of the moon
[...]
. AD 884.

U885.1 Jump to heading ¶

Tuileflaith, abbess of Cell Dara, fell asleep; and Scannal, bishop of Cell Dara, dies.

U885.2 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall son of Cinaed, king of Cenél Laegaire, died in clerical life.

U885.3 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Tuile son of Fechtnach, superior of Glas Noíden, dies.

U885.4 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Pátraic son of Mael Curarda, king of the Airgialla, was killed by his associates.

U885.5 Jump to heading ¶

A solar eclipse, and stars were seen in the heavens.

U885.6 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Dúin son of Aengus, king of Caille Follamhain, dies.

U885.7 Jump to heading ¶

Cormac, superior of Cluain Iraird and bishop of Dam Liac, rests after prolonged illness.

U885.8 Jump to heading ¶

A child at Craeb Laisre spoke two months after its birth, which had not been heard of from ancient times.

U885.9 Jump to heading ¶

Muiredach son of Bran, king of Laigin and superior of Cell Dara, fell asleep.

U885.10 Jump to heading ¶

Secret murder was committed in Cell Dara.

U885.11 Jump to heading ¶

Mugrón son of Cenn Faelad, superior of Cluain Ferta Brénainn, dies.

p.343

U886.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January twenty-first of the moon.
[...]
. AD 885.

U886.1 Jump to heading ¶

  1. (The choice earth has not covered,

To Temair's multitudes there shall not come,

Ireland of the great territories(?) shall not contain

A man like the pure and gentle Mael Muru. 2. There has never tasted death fearlessly,

Nor reached the known dead,

The cultivator's soil has never covered

A more wonderful keeper of tradition.)

  1. (Alas, o holy Patrick

That your prayers did not protect it

When the foreigners with their axes

Were smiting your oratory!)

  1. (The son of Der bFáil, fighting for Brega's plain,

Was wont to smash every deceitful band,

Generous Mael Finnia, mighty and valiant,

A stout hero, very noble and warlike. 2. We had a king (no risky proceeding)

Who was a champion towering over the assembly of Emain,

A man—I say it without risk of contradiction—

Who alone was a match for all Ireland.

p.355

  1. Mael Finnia, a man without arrogance(?),

Brega's lord, a flame who swept over high places,

Comely was this choice king of noble bounty,

Crinna's sovereign, peace-loving though fierce in battle.)

Mael Martain, superior of Lugbad, rested.

U908.3 Jump to heading ¶

A battle was fought between the men of Mumu, the Leth Cuinn, and the Laigin in Mag Ailbi on the feast of Dagán of Inber Dáile, i.e. on Tuesday the Ides 13th of September, the thirteenth of the moon, and Cormac son of Cuilennán, king of Caisel, was killed there together with other distinguished kings. These are: Fogartach son of Suibne, king of Ciarraige, Cellach son of Cerball, king of Osraige, Ailill son of Eógan, superior of the Trian of Corcach, and Colmán, superior of Cenn Eitig. Flann son of Mael Sechnaill, king of Temair, Cerball son of Muirecán, king of Laigin, and Cathal son of Conchobor, king of Connacht, were victors.—The battle of Belach Mugna.

Diarmait, superior of Daire Calgaig, rested in peace.

U908.5 Jump to heading ¶

The anchorite Cormac, superior of Druim Mór, dies.

Mael Ograi son of Congalach, king of Loch Gabor, was deceitfully killed by Fogartach son of Tolarg.

  1. (Muiredach,

Why do you not lament him, friends?

His death is good cause for a general mortality,

It is as a cloud reaching to the saints of heaven. 2. This distinguished man is a great loss,

The magnificent jewel of choice

Who was the light of every musical company.)

A dark and rainy year. A comet appeared.

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 912 alias 913.

Tipraite son of Mael Finn, superior of Imlech Ibuir, Mael Muire, daughter of Cinaed, son of Ailpín, and Ethelwald, king of the Saxons of the North, die.

U913.2 Jump to heading ¶

Congalach son of Gairbith, king of Conaille, was killed in the ninth month after he had sacked the abbot's house in Druim Inasclainn and killed the son of Mael Mórda and Muiredach son of Cormac, superior of Druim Inasclainn.

U913.3 Jump to heading ¶

Cuilennán son of Mael Brigte dies at the end of this same year.

U913.4 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad grandson of Mael Sechnaill and Mael Mithig son of Flannacán inflicted a battle-rout on Fogartach son of Tolarg, king of southern Brega, and Lorcán son of Donnchad and the Laigin, and they left behind many, both dead and prisoners.

U913.5 Jump to heading ¶

The heathens inflicted a battle-rout on the crew of a new fleet of the Ulaid, on the coast of England, and many fell, including Cumuscach son of Mael Mocheirgi, son of the king of Leth Cathail.

U913.6 Jump to heading ¶

Niall son of Aed led an expedition to Connacht and inflicted a battle-rout on the warriors of the north of Connacht, i.e. on the Uí Amalgada and the men of Umall, and they left behind a very large number either dead or captured, including Mael Cluiche son of Conchobor.

U913.7 Jump to heading ¶

A dark and rainy year.

U913.8 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Brigte son of Tornán went to Mumu to ransom a Welsh pilgrim.

U914.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 913 alias 914.

U914.1 Jump to heading ¶

Southern Brega and southern Cianacht were invaded by Flann son of Mael Sechnaill. Many churches were profaned by him.

U914.2 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Brigte son of Giblechán, king of Conaille, was mortally wounded by the Uí Echach in the fourth month of his reign.

U914.3 Jump to heading ¶

Niall son of Aed made an expedition into Dál Araidi in the month of June. Loingsech grandson of Lethlabar, king of Dál Araidi, came upon him at Fregabal and was defeated, and left behind on his retreat Flathruae grandson of Lethlabar, his kinsman. Aed son of Eochucán, king of the Province, and Loingsech, king of Dál Araidi, met them again at Carn Éirenn and were defeated. Cerrán

p.363

son of Colman, chief of Cenél Maelchi, and the son of Allacán son of Laíchthechán, and others, were left behind. Aed, however, returning from the flight with a very few, and fiercely resisting during the flight, wiped out some of Niall's soldiers. His son Dubgall was wounded and escaped.

U914.4 Jump to heading ¶

A naval battle at Manu between Barid son of Oitir and Ragnall grandson of Ímar, in which Barid and almost all his army were destroyed.

U914.5 Jump to heading ¶

A great new fleet of the heathens on Loch dá Caech.

U914.6 Jump to heading ¶

Peace was made at Telach Óc on the Kalends 1st of November between Niall son of Aed, king of Ailech, and Aed, king of the Province.

U914.7 Jump to heading ¶

A Northern army was led by Niall son of Aed to Mide in the month of December. He halted at Grellach Eilte to the west of Crosa Caíl. A large force left the encampment at his order to seek corn and firewood. Aengus son of Mael Sechnaill, as well as his kinsmen and a large force of the men of Mide, came upon them and left dead forty-five of them, including Coinnecán son of Muirchertach and Fergal son of Aengus and Uathmarán son of Aileb and Erudán son of Gairbíth, chief of Uí Bresail Macha, and Mael Ruanaid son of Cumuscach, chief of Síl Duibthire, and Mael Brigte son of Aedacán, and the son of Erumain son of Aed, and Fiachra son of Cellachán, and Mael Muire son of Flannacán, heir designate of Airgialla.

  1. (Grief came from cold Grellach Eilte—

We encountered a troop beside it;

Cormacán said to Niall:

‘Let us not be thrown back, let us go forward as nobles.)’

U915.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 914 alias 915.

Aengus grandson of Mael Sechnaill, heir designate of Temair, dies on the seventh of the Ides 7th of February, the third feria.

  1. (A blessing on the hand of Cern son of Bern

Who killed the noble and illustrious Aengus of Fál:

It was a goodly assault with sharp weapons

Which avenged splendid Aed Alláin.)

U915.2 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall son of Aed, king of Ailech, dies in penitence at the spring equinox 21 March.

p.365

U915.3 Jump to heading ¶

Flann son of Mael Sechnaill was rebelled against by his sons, that is, by Donnchad and Conchobor, and they harried Mide as far as Loch Rí. Niall son of Aed, king of Ailech, brought a northern army and exacted a pledge from Donnchad and Conchobor that they would obey their father, and made a truce between Mide and Brega.

U915.4 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Ciaráin son of Eochucán, superior of Cluain Eois, and bishop of Ard Macha, died in the 50th year of his age.

U915.5 Jump to heading ¶

Scannlán, superior of Tamlacht, and Scannlán, superior of In Chongbáil of Glenn Suiligi, die in Christ.

U915.6 Jump to heading ¶

Ruarc son of Mael Brigte, king of Múscraige Tíre, was mortally wounded by treachery and cunning by the Uí Dúngalaig.

U915.7 Jump to heading ¶

A great and frequent increase in the number of heathens arriving at Loch dá Chaech, and the laity and clergy of Mumu were plundered by them.

U916.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 915 alias 916.

U916.1 Jump to heading ¶

Flann son of Mael Sechnaill son of Mael Ruanaid son of Donnchad king of Temair, having reigned 36 years 6 months and 5 days, dies in the 68th year of his age, about the seventh hour of day, on the seventh feria, the eighth of the Kalends of June 25 May.

U916.2 Jump to heading ¶

Fogartach son of Tolarg, king of southern Brega, dies.

U916.3 Jump to heading ¶

Ainnle son of Cathán, king of Uaithne of Cliú, was put to death by the foreigners of Loch dá Chaech.

U916.4 Jump to heading ¶

Aed son of Ailill, abbot of Cluain Ferta Brénainn, Conligán son of Draignén, chief of Uí Lomáin Gaela, and Martain, abbot of Ros Comáin, die.

U916.5 Jump to heading ¶

Niall son of Aed became king of Temair and held the Fair of Tailtiu, which had been neglected for a long time.

U916.6 Jump to heading ¶

The foreigners of Loch dá Chaech continued to harry Mumu and Laigin.

U916.7 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Barrfhinn, priest of Cluain Moccu Nóis, dies.

U916.8 Jump to heading ¶

Ard Macha was burned by lightning on the fifth of the Kalends of May 27 April, i.e. the southern part of it, with the Toí and the Saball and the kitchen and the whole of the abbot's close.

U916.9 Jump to heading ¶

Coblaith daughter of Dub Dúin, successor of Brigit, rested.

p.367

U917.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 916 alias 917.

U917.1 Jump to heading ¶

Snow and extreme cold and unnatural ice this year, so that the chief lakes and rivers of Ireland were passable, and causing death to cattle, birds and salmon. Horrible portents also: the heavens seemed to glow with comets; and a mass of fire appeared with thunder in the west beyond Ireland, and it went eastwards over the sea.

U917.2 Jump to heading ¶

Sitriuc, grandson of Ímar, landed with his fleet at Cenn Fuait on the coast of Laigin. Ragnall, grandson of Ímar, with his second fleet moved against the foreigners of Loch dá Chaech. A slaughter of the foreigners at Neimlid in Muma. The Eóganacht and the Ciarraige made another slaughter.

U917.3 Jump to heading ¶

Niall son of Aed, king of Ireland, led an army of the southern and northern Uí Néill to Munster to make war on the heathens. He halted on the 22nd day of the month of August at Topar Glethrach in Mag Feimin. The heathens had come into the district on the same day. The Irish attacked them between the hour of tierce and midday and they fought until eventide, and about a hundred men, the majority foreigners, fell between them. Reinforcements(?) came from the camp of the foreigners to aid their fellows. The Irish turned back to their camp in face of the last reinforcement, i.e. Ragnall, king of the dark foreigners, accompanied by a large force of foreigners. Niall son of Aed proceeded with a small number against the heathens, so that God prevented a great slaughter of the others through him. After that Niall remained twenty nights encamped against the heathens. He sent word to the Laigin that they should lay siege to the encampment from a distance. They were routed by Sitriuc grandson of Ímar in the battle of Cenn Fuait, where five hundred, or somewhat more, fell. And there fell too Ugaire son of Ailill, king of Laigin, Mael Mórda son of Muirecán, king of eastern Life, Mael Maedóc son of Diarmait, a scholar and bishop of Laigin, Ugrán son of Cennéitig, king of Laíges, and other leaders and nobles.

U917.4 Jump to heading ¶

Sitriuc grandson of Ímar entered Áth Cliath.

U917.5 Jump to heading ¶

Eithne daughter of Aed died truly penitent on the feast of Martin.

U918.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 917 alias 918.

U918.1 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Eóin, superior and bishop of Ros Cré, and Éicnech, superior of Ára Airthir, died.

p.369

U918.2 Jump to heading ¶

Dainél of Cluain Coirpthe, a wonderful custodian of historical lore, fell asleep in peace.

U918.3 Jump to heading ¶

Muirenn, daughter of Suart, abbess of Cell Dara, rested.

U918.4 Jump to heading ¶

The foreigners of Loch dá Chaech, i.e. Ragnall, king of the dark foreigners, and the two jarls, Oitir and Gragabai, forsook Ireland and proceeded afterwards against the men of Scotland. The men of Scotland, moreover, moved against them and they met on the bank of the Tyne in northern Saxonland. The heathens formed themselves into four battalions: a battalion with Gothfrith grandson of Ímar, a battalion with the two jarls, and a battalion with the young lords. There was also a battalion in ambush with Ragnall, which the men of Scotland did not see. The Scotsmen routed the three battalions which they saw, and made a very great slaughter of the heathens, including Oitir and Gragabai. Ragnall, however, then attacked in the rear of the Scotsmen, and made a slaughter of them, although none of their kings or earls was cut off. Nightfall caused the battle to be broken off.

U918.5 Jump to heading ¶

Ethelfled, a very famous queen of the Saxons, dies.

U918.6 Jump to heading ¶

Warfare between Niall son of Aed, king of Temair, and Sitriuc grandson of Ímar.

U918.7 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Mithig son of Flannacán, king of Cnogba, went over to the heathens with a view to defending northern Brega from(?) the heathens, which availed him not at all.

U919.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 918 alias 919.

U919.1 Jump to heading ¶

Easter on the seventh of the Kalends of May 25 April and Low Sunday on the second day of summer.

U919.2 Jump to heading ¶

Aed grandson of Mael Sechnaill was blinded by his kinsman, Donnchad, king of Mide.

U919.3 Jump to heading ¶

The heathens won a battle against the Irish at Duiblinn in which fell Niall Glúndub son of Aed, king of Ireland, in the third year of his reign, on the fourth feria, the eighteenth of the Kalends of October 14 Sept., and here fell also Aed son of Eochucán, king of Conchobor's Province, and Mael Mithig son of Flannacán, king of Brega, and Conchobor grandson of Mael Sechnaill, heir designate or king of Temair, and Flaithbertach son of Domnall, heir designate of the North, and the son of Dub Sínaig, i.e. Mael Craibe, king of Airgialla, and many other nobles.—The battle of Áth Cliath won by the foreigners.

p.371

  1. (Mournful today is virginal Ireland

Without a mighty king in command of hostages;

It is to view the heaven and not to see the sun

To behold Niall's plain without Niall. 2. It has no mirth (a possession of real worth),

It has no peace nor pleasure in a throng,

It is powerless to enjoy itself at a fair,

Since he who brings tears of sorrow has cast it down. 3. Sad indeed, o yellowing plain of Brega,

O lovely desirable land,

That you have parted from your lordly king,

That glorious deadly Niall has left you. 4. Where now are the princes of the western world,

Where now the horror of every clang of arms

Since valiant Niall of Cnucha

Has brought desolation to his great cantred?)

U919.4 Jump to heading ¶

Cet son of Flaithbertach, king of Corcu Mruad, and Tigernach grandson of Cléirech, king of Uí Fhiachrach of Aidne, died.

U920.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 919 alias 920.

U920.1 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Muire, superior of Ard Brecán, dies.

U920.2 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad, grandson of Mael Sechnaill, inflicted a battle-rout on the heathens, in which a very large number were slaughtered.

U920.3 Jump to heading ¶

Finchar, bishop and excellent scribe of Damliac, rested happily.

U920.4 Jump to heading ¶

Scannal of Ros Cré, scribe of Cluain Moccu Nóis, rested.

U920.5 Jump to heading ¶

Sitriuc, grandson of Ímar, abandoned Áth Cliath, through the power of God.

U920.6 Jump to heading ¶

The stone church of Cenannas was broken down by the heathens, and a large number suffered violent death in it. The stone church of Tuilén was burned on the same day.

U920.7 Jump to heading ¶

Cormac son of Cuilennán, king of the Déisi of Mumu, was killed.

U921.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 920 alias 921.

U921.1 Jump to heading ¶

Maenach son of Siadal, successor of Comgall, chief master of erudition in the island of Ireland, fell asleep.

U921.2 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall grandson of Mael Sechnaill was deceitfully killed by his brother Donnchad, which was fitting.

U921.3 Jump to heading ¶

Ciarán, abbot of Daiminis, rests.

U921.4 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Sechnaill grandson of Flann, heir designate of Temair, Fiachra son of Cathalán, king of Caille Fallamhain, and Ragnall grandson of Ímar, king of the fair foreigners and the dark foreigners—all died.

U921.5 Jump to heading ¶

Gothfrith grandson of Ímar entered Áth Cliath.

U921.6 Jump to heading ¶

Cinaed son of Domnall, superior of Daire Calgaig and Druim Tuama, and chief counsellor of Cenél Conaill of the North, died.

U921.7 Jump to heading ¶

A fleet of the foreigners came into Loch Febail, i.e. Acolb with thirty-two ships. Cennrig was quickly(?) and completely abandoned by them, except for a few who remained behind in it through sloth. Fergal son of Domnall, king of the North, was in hostilities with them, and killed the crew of one of their ships and wrecked the ship and took its booty. Another naval force was at Cenn Magair on the coast of Tír Conaill, i.e. under the son of Uathmarán son of Barid, with twenty ships.

U921.8 Jump to heading ¶

Ard Macha was invaded by the foreigners of Áth Cliath, i.e. by Gothfrith grandson of Ímar, with his army, on the fourth of the Ides 10th of November, the Saturday before the feast of Martin, and the prayer-houses with their complement of culdees and sick he spared from destruction, and also the monastery, save for a few dwellings which were burned through carelessness. They harried widely on all sides, westwards to Inis Ua Labrada, eastwards to the Banna, and northwards to Mag Ilesen. But Muirchertach son of Niall and Aignert son of Murchad came upon the force that had gone north, defeating them, and they left many dead behind, only a few escaping in the dim light of dusk.

U921.9 Jump to heading ¶

A lunar eclipse on the third feria, the fifteenth of the Kalends of January at the first hour of night.

U921.10 Jump to heading ¶

Flaithbertach son of Muirchertach abbot of Cluain Mór dies.

  1. Of what value is the possession (?) of undiminished wealth,

Of what value the repute of competent scholars,

Since fair hospitable Flaithbertach

Has parted with the preferment of Cluain Mór?

p.375

Kalends of January
[...]

Mael Póil son of Ailill, scholar and bishop of the descendants of Aed of Sláine, Tadc son of Faelán, king of Uí Chennselaig, Cernach son of Flann, superior of Lann Léire and steward of the community of Ard Macha from Belach Dúin to the sea and from Bóinn to Casán, and chief counsellor and consultant of the men of all Brega—all die.

U922.2 Jump to heading ¶

Ruman, bishop of Cluain Iraird, Ferdálach, bishop of Cluain Moccu Nóis, Loingsech son of Aenacán, household steward of Dam Liac, Colgu son of Mael Sempuil, abbot of Sláine—all died.

U922.3 Jump to heading ¶

The fleet of Luimnech, that is, of Ailche's son, went on Loch Rí, plundered Cluain Moccu Nóis, and all the islands on Loch Rí, and took great booty in gold, silver and much treasure.

[...]

U923.3 Jump to heading ¶

The plundering of Fir Arda and Lann Léire and Fir Rois in the same month.

U923.6 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Cluiche son of Conchobor, heir designate of Connacht, was treacherously killed.

U923.8 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Calann, superior of Dísert Diarmata, rested.

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 923 alias 924.

A naval force of the foreigners went on Loch Éirne, and they ravaged the islands of the lake and the surrounding peoples, to and fro. They left Loch Éirne in the summer following.

U924.2 Jump to heading ¶

Foreigners went on Loch Cuan and Mael Dúin son of Aed, heir designate of the Province, fell by them. A great new fleet of the foreigners foundered at Fertas Rudraige, and nine hundred or more were drowned.

U924.3 Jump to heading ¶

Gothfrith, grandson of Ímar, made an expedition from Áth Cliath to Luimnech, and a very large company of his followers were left behind dead with Ailche's son.

U924.4 Jump to heading ¶

Mochta, bishop of Uí Néill and priest of Ard Macha, rested in peace.

U924.5 Jump to heading ¶

Muiredach son of Domnall, tanist-abbot of Ard Macha, and chief steward of the southern Uí Néill, and successor of Buite son of Brónach, chief counsellor of the men of all Brega, both laymen and clerics, departed this life on the fifth day before the Kalends of December 27 Nov..

U924.6 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Mórda son of Congal, superior of Daiminis, rested.

Kalends of January
[...]

U925.1 Jump to heading ¶

U925.2 Jump to heading ¶

U925.3 Jump to heading ¶

U925.4 Jump to heading ¶

The sacking of Dún Sobairche by the foreigners of Loch Cuan, in which many men were killed or captured.

U926.2 Jump to heading ¶

U926.3 Jump to heading ¶

Colmán, superior of Cluain Iraird and Cluain Moccu Nóis, and a scribe and bishop, rested in Christ.

U926.4 Jump to heading ¶

Fergus son of Duiligén, king of Lurg, was killed by the men of Breifne.

The fleet of Loch Cuan, i.e. under Alpthann son of Gothfrith, landed at Linn Duachaill on the day before the Nones 4th of September.

U926.6 Jump to heading ¶

Muirchertach son of Niall inflicted a rout at the bridge of Cluain na Cruimther on the fifth feria, the fifth of the Kalends of January 28 Dec., in which fell Alpthann son of Gothfrith, with a great destruction of his army. Half of them were besieged for a week at Áth Cruithne, until Gothfrith, king of the foreigners, came from Áth Cliath to relieve them.

[...]

U927.5 Jump to heading ¶

U927.6 Jump to heading ¶

Céile, successor of Comgall, scribe and anchorite and apostolic doctor of all Ireland, rested happily at Rome on his pilgrimage, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October 14 Sept., in the 59th year of his age.

  1. (Thrice nine and nine hundred years

Are reckoned by clear rules

Since the year of Christ's birth (a benign occurrence)

Until the holy death of the cleric Céile.)

U929.4 Jump to heading ¶

An expedition by Donnchad to Liathdruim against Niall's son.

  1. (Let someone tell the brown-haired Donnchad,

The palisade-like fighter who hews down races,

Though Liathdruim may lie before him,

There is an angry fellow there.)

Kalends of January
[...]

Gothfrith, grandson of Ímar, with the foreigners of Áth Cliath, razed Derc Ferna—something unheard of from ancient times.

U930.1 Jump to heading ¶

Flann of Fobar, a bishop and anchorite, rests happily at an old age.

U930.2 Jump to heading ¶

Foreigners on Loch nEchach, and their naval camp was at Ruib Mena.

Foreigners on Loch Bethrach in Osraige.

large number of Saxons fell on the other side, but Athelstan, king of the Saxons, enjoyed a great victory.

Fedach superior of Sláine, died.

U938.4 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad son of Flann and Muirchertach son of Niall made preparations for a battle, and God brought them to peace.

U938.5 Jump to heading ¶

Amlaíb son of Gothfrith in Áth Cliath again.

U938.6 Jump to heading ¶

Cell Cuilinn was plundered by Amlaíb grandson of Ímar—something unheard of from ancient times. Donnchad grandson of Mael Sechnaill, king of Temair, and Muirchertach son of Niall, king of Ailech, led an army to besiege the foreigners of Áth Cliath, and they ravaged from Áth Cliath to Áth Truisten.

U938.7 Jump to heading ¶

Conchobor son of Mael Cian, king of Uí Fhailgi, was killed by the Laigin.

U939.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 938 alias 939.

U939.1 Jump to heading ¶

The plundering of Cell Chuilinn by the foreigners of Áth Cliath—something which did not often happen.

U939.2 Jump to heading ¶

Críchán son of Mael Muire, king of Uí Fhiachrach, dies.

U939.3 Jump to heading ¶

Ailech was sacked against Muirchertach son of Niall, and he was brought off to the fleet, but ransomed himself afterwards.

U939.4 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad led an army into Brega, and Finnubair Abae was plundered, and the priest killed within the church, and another person besides.

U939.5 Jump to heading ¶

Congalach son of Mael Mithig defeated the Gailenga Móra and the Gailenga Beca at Áth dá Loarc, and many fell there.

U939.6 Jump to heading ¶

Athelstan, king of the Saxons, pillar of.the dignity of the western world, died an untroubled death.

U939.7 Jump to heading ¶

Fínnechta son of Cellach, coarb of Daire, rested in Christ.

p.389

U940.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January, eighteenth of the moon,
[...]
. AD 939 alias 940.

U940.1 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad and Muirchertach led an army to the Laigin and to Mumu, and both took their hostages.

U940.2 Jump to heading ¶

Suibne son of Cú Bretan was killed by the foreigners.

U940.3 Jump to heading ¶

Niall son of Fergal was wounded and drowned, that is, by Muirchertach son of Niall.

U940.4 Jump to heading ¶

Flann daughter of Donnchad, queen of Ailech, dies.

U940.5 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad made a foray into Brega and plundered Lann Léire.

U940.6 Jump to heading ¶

Repose of Muiredach, successor of Comgall.

U941.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January, twenty-ninth of the moon
[...]
. AD 940 alias 941.

U941.1 Jump to heading ¶

Severe frost so that the ice on lakes and streams was passable.

U941.2 Jump to heading ¶

Birth of Brian son of Cennéitig.

U941.3 Jump to heading ¶

An expedition i.e. the expedition in the frost(?) was made by Muirchertach, and he plundered Mide and Ú Fhailgi, and went into Osraige, obtaining their submission. He ravaged the Déisi, and brought Cellachán, king of Caisel, in submission to Donnchad.

U941.4 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Ruanaid son of Flann, i.e. heir designate of Ailech, was killed by the Cenél Conaill.

U941.5 Jump to heading ¶

Eochu son of Scannal, superior of Imlech Ibuir, dies.

U941.6 Jump to heading ¶

Aenacán, priest of Dún Lethglaise, dies.

U942.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January, tenth of the moon
[...]
. AD 941 alias 942.

U942.1 Jump to heading ¶

Dúnchad son of Suthainén, bishop of Cluain Moccu Nóis, died.

U942.2 Jump to heading ¶

Faelán son of Muiredach, king of Laigin, dies.

U942.3 Jump to heading ¶

The Uí Fhailgi inflicted a battle-rout on the foreigners of Áth Cliath—but this happened in the previous year.

U942.4 Jump to heading ¶

Dún Lethglaise was plundered by the foreigners. God and Patrick avenged it on them, causing them to go overseas and taking their island from them so that their king stole away and was killed by the Irish on land.

U942.5 Jump to heading ¶

Two sons of Lorcán son of Donnchad were killed by Congalach son of Mael Mithig.

U942.6 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Mochta, superior of Cluain Iraird, rested.

U942.7 Jump to heading ¶

Cluain Moccu Nóis and Cell Dara were ravaged by the heathens of Áth Cliath.

p.391

U943.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January, twenty-first of the moon
[...]
. AD 942 alias 943.

U943.1 Jump to heading ¶

The Leth Cathail inflicted a rout on the foreigners of Loch Cuan, in which nearly all were destroyed.

U943.2 Jump to heading ¶

Muirchertach son of Niall, i.e. Muirchertach of the Leather Cloaks, king of Ailech and the Hector of the western world, was killed by the heathens, i.e. by Blacair son of Gothfrith, king of the foreigner, at Glas Liatháin beside Cluain Chaín, in Fir Rois, on the first feria, fourth of the Kalends of March 26 Feb.. Ard Macha was plundered by the same foreigners on the following day, the third of the Kalends of March.

  1. (Vengeance and ruin have come to rest

On the race of Conn's children for ever:

It were grievous that Muirchertach lives no more,

The land of the famous Irish is orphaned.)

U943.3 Jump to heading ¶

Lorcán, son of Faelán, king of Laigin, was killed by the foreigners.

U943.4 Jump to heading ¶

Cellach son of Béc, king of Dál Araidi, was treacherously killed by his people.

U944.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 943 alias 944.

U944.1 Jump to heading ¶

Flaithbertach son of Inmainén, chief, rested in peace.

U944.2 Jump to heading ¶

Cairpre son of Mael Pátraic, king of Uí, Liatháin, and Finn son of Mután, king of Corcu Laígdi, were killed by the men of Mag Féine.

U944.3 Jump to heading ¶

Congalach son of Mael Mithig and Braen son of Mael Mórda, king of Laigin, plundered Áth Cliath, and took away valuables, and treasure, and much booty.

U944.4 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad son of Flann son of Mael Sechnaill son of Mael Ruanaid son of Donnchad, king of Temair, dies after spending 25 years as king.

U944.5 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Feichéne, successor of Finnia, rested.

U944.6 Jump to heading ¶

Dúngal son of Cathán fell asleep in Christ.

U944.7 Jump to heading ¶

The battle of Gort Rotacháin was won by Cellachán against Tuadmumu, and many fell in it.

p.393

U945.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 944 alias 945.

U945.1 Jump to heading ¶

Abnormally severe frost so that the lakes and rivers were passable on foot.

U945.2 Jump to heading ¶

The foreigners of Loch nEchach were killed by Domnall son of Muirchertach and by his kinsman, i.e. Flaithbertach, and their fleet was destroyed.

U945.3 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Tuile son of Dúnán, successor of Tigernach and Cairnech, dies an untroubled death.

U945.4 Jump to heading ¶

Aurchath son of Murchad, king of the west of Connacht, died.

U945.5 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Dúin son of Gairbíth, prior of Ard Macha, died.

U945.6 Jump to heading ¶

Blacair gave up Áth Cliath and Amlaíb succeeded him.

U945.7 Jump to heading ¶

A band of Ua Canannáin's followers were killed by Congalach and Amlaíb Cuaráin in Conaille.

U946.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 945 alias 946.

U946.1 Jump to heading ¶

Cluain Moccu Nóis was plundered by the foreigners of Áth Cliath, and also the churches of the men of Mide.

U946.2 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Bethach, superior of Daiminis, dies.

U947.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 946 alias 947.

U947.1 Jump to heading ¶

Ruaidrí ua Canannáin led an army to Sláine, and the foreigners and Irish, i.e. Congalach son of Mael Mithig and Amlaíb Cuaráin, came upon him, and the foreigners of Áth Cliath were defeated, and many of them killed and drowned.

U947.2 Jump to heading ¶

The Cenél Eógain gave the full measure of the Finnfaídech of pure silver to Patrick.

U947.3 Jump to heading ¶

Scolaige ua hAedacáin, king of Dartraige, and Gairbíth son of Muiredach, heir designate of Uí Chremthainn, and Aed son of Tigernán ua Ruairc were killed in battle in a counterattack.

U947.4 Jump to heading ¶

Braen son of Mael Mórda, king of the Laigin, was killed on a foray in Osraige.

U947.5 Jump to heading ¶

Cathusach son of Ailche, bishop of Cenél Eógain, dies.

U948.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 947 alias 948.

U948.1 Jump to heading ¶

Blacair son of Gothfrith, king of the foreigners, was killed by Congalach son of Mael Mithig, and sixteen hundred were also killed or taken captive.

U948.2 Jump to heading ¶

(Birth of Mael Sechnaill son of Domnall.)

p.395

U948.3 Jump to heading ¶

Ainmire ua hAdlai, successor of Ciarán son of the wright, died.

U948.4 Jump to heading ¶

Colmán son of Mael Pátraic, superior of Sláine, was taken prisoner by the foreigners, and died on their hands.

U948.5 Jump to heading ¶

Gormlaith, daughter of Flann son of Mael Sechnaill, died in penitence.

U949.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 948 alias 949.

U949.1 Jump to heading ¶

Matudán son of Aed and Niall grandson of Erulb made an expedition and plundered Conaille and Druim Inasclainn and Inis Caín Dega.

U949.2 Jump to heading ¶

Ua Canannáin made a foray and plundered Fir Lí and killed Flaithbertach ua Néill.

U949.3 Jump to heading ¶

Aedán of Tuaim da Gualann rested in Christ.

U949.4 Jump to heading ¶

Fogartach son of Donnocán, king of Airgialla, dies in penitence.

U949.5 Jump to heading ¶

Congalach son of Mael Mithig made an expedition and ravaged Uí Meith and Fernmag.

U950.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 949 alias 950.

U950.1 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad son of Domnall, king of Mide, was killed by his kinsmen.

U950.2 Jump to heading ¶

Hywel, king of Wales, dies.

U950.3 Jump to heading ¶

Scothíne, superior of Dairmag, Mael Finnáin, bishop of Cell Dara, and Cleirchéne son of Conallán, superior of Daire Calgaig, rested in peace.

U950.4 Jump to heading ¶

Matudán son of Aed was killed by the Uí Echach, i.e. by the sons of Bran, but God avenged him within a short time by bringing about their deaths.

U950.5 Jump to heading ¶

Ruaidrí ua Canannáin, i.e. heir designate of Ireland, was killed by the foreigners after he had beleaguered Mide and Brega for six months and had inflicted a slaughter on the foreigners, to the number of two thousand or more. Niall ua Canannáin and a few others were also slain in a counterattack.—The battle of Muine Brócáin.

U950.6 Jump to heading ¶

An abnormally great mast-crop.

U950.7 Jump to heading ¶

The bell-house of Sláine was burned by the foreigners of Áth Cliath. The founder's episcopal staff, and the best of all bells, the lector Caenachair and a large number with him, were all burned.

p.397

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 950 alias 951.

U951.1 Jump to heading ¶

Mac Étig son of Cuilennán, king of Conaille, died.

U951.2 Jump to heading ¶

Guaire ua Forannáin, superior of Ard Sratha, dies.

U951.3 Jump to heading ¶

Gothfrith son of Sitriuc with the foreigners of Áth Cliath plundered Cenannas and Domnach Pátraic and Ard Brecáin and Tuileáin and Cell Scíre and other churches. From Cenannas they were all plundered, and three thousand men or more were taken captive and a great spoil of cattle and horses and gold and silver was taken away.

U951.4 Jump to heading ¶

Aed son of Mael Ruanaid, Béc son of Donn Cuan, king of Tethba, Cennéitig son of Lorcán, king of Tuadmumu, Gairbíth son of Lorcán, king of Fir Leamna, died.

U951.5 Jump to heading ¶

Niall Mothlach was wickedly killed by the Cairpre.

U951.6 Jump to heading ¶

A mortality of bees.

U951.7 Jump to heading ¶

A great outbreak of leprosy among the foreigners of Áth Cliath, and dysentery.

U952.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 951 alias 952.

Scannal, superior of Domnach Sechnaill, Flann, superior of Druim Cliab, Constantine son of Aed, king of Scotland, Ferdomnach, successor of Ciarán, died.

U952.2 Jump to heading ¶

The foreigners won a battle over the men of Scotland and the Welsh and the Saxons.

U952.3 Jump to heading ¶

Flann ua Cléirig, king of the south of Connacht, Domnall son of Donnchad, heir designate of Temair, Céile the leper and anchorite, Flann son of Mael Fiachrach, superior of Mag eter di Glais, died.

U953.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 952 alias 953.

U953.1 Jump to heading ¶

Cluain Moccu Nóis was plundered by the men of Mumu, accompanied by foreigners.

Mael Cothaid, successor of Comgall and Mo-Cholmóc, died.

U953.3 Jump to heading ¶

Gailenga was plundered by the Uí Chremthainn. Domnall came upon Muirchertach, and they left behind many heads.

U953.4 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Martain son of Maenach, Ruadacán son of Eitigén, king of eastern Gailenga, Mael Pátraic son of Coscán, lector of Ard Macha, Mael Muire, superior of Tech Féthgna, Cenn Faelad, superior of Saiger, Diarmait son of Torpaid, superior of Les Mór Mo-Chutu, Dub Inse, bishop of Bennchor, died.

p.399

U954.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 953 alias 954.

U954.1 Jump to heading ¶

Flannacán son of Allchú, successor of Mac Nisse and Colmán of Ela, died.

U954.2 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Coluim son of Domnall, king of Scotland, was killed.

U954.3 Jump to heading ¶

Conn son of Erudán son of Gairbíth, king of Mag Dumai, was killed.

U954.4 Jump to heading ¶

A great murrain of cattle throughout Ireland.

U954.5 Jump to heading ¶

Ua Ruairc inflicted a great slaughter on the Cairpre and Tethba, and ua Ciardai, king of Cairpri, fell.

U954.6 Jump to heading ¶

Céilechair, successor of Ciarán and Finnian, and Robartach, successor of Colum Cille and Adamnán, rested in Christ.

U954.7 Jump to heading ¶

Niall ua Tolairg, Cellachán, king of Caisel, and Rechtabra, superior of Cell Achaid, died.

U954.8 Jump to heading ¶

Bran son of Domnall, king of Cenél Laegaire of Brega, was killed.

U955.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January sixth feria, fourth of the moon. AD 954 alias 955.

U955.1 Jump to heading ¶

Aengus son of Cú Loingse, superior of Mag Bile, and Aengus son of Mael Brigte, superior of Dam Liac, die.

U955.2 Jump to heading ¶

Aléne, king of Mugdorna Maigen and Mugdorna of Brega, and Innéirge son of Mochán, fell on Congalach's march into Connacht.

U955.3 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall son of Muirchertach led a force, with ships, from Tuag Inbir, on Loch nEchach and Daball, across Airgialla, on Loch Éirne, then on Loch Uachtair, and he plundered Bréifne and took hostages from ua Ruairc.

U956.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January seventh feria, fifteenth of the moon. AD 955 alias 956.

Mael Pátraic son of Cú Bretan, superior of Sláine, Aengus son of Nocán, successor of Féichéne, and Gaíthéne the learned, bishop of Dún Lethglaise, died.

U956.2 Jump to heading ¶

Tadc son of Cathal, king of Connacht, died.

U956.3 Jump to heading ¶

Congalach son of Mael Mithig son of Flannacán son of Cellach son of Congalagh son of Conaing of Cuirrech son of Congalach son of Aed of Sláine, king of Ireland, was killed by the foreigners of Áth Cliath and by the Laigin at Tech Giurann in Laigin; and Aed son of Aichid, king of Tethba, and many others were also killed.

p.401

U956.4 Jump to heading ¶

Maenach, successor of Finnia and lector of Ard Macha, Mael Brigte son of Erudán, successor of Mac Nise and Colmán of Ela, and Muiredach son of Éicnechán, die.

U956.5 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall begins to reign.

U957.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]

Cathasach son of Duiligén from Druim Torraid successor of Patrick and a learned Irish bishop, rested in Jesus Christ.

Mael Fothartaig, king of Caisel, Colmán son of Congal, successor of Mo-Laise, Eochu son of Anluan, king of Loch gCal, Scannal son of Luachdub, coarb of Liss Críst (?), die.

Mael Coluim ua Canannáin, king of Cenél Conaill, Mochta son of Gormacán, and Flann ua hAedacáin, superior of Glenn dá Locha, died.

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 957 alias 958.

Flann son of Mochloinges, successor of Tigernach and Mael Dóid, died.

Tanaide son of Odar, coarb of Bennchor, was killed by the foreigners.

U958.3 Jump to heading ¶

Niall ua Eruilb.

Tuathal son of Úgaire, king of Laigin, dies.

U958.5 Jump to heading ¶

Lugaid son of Colgu, superior of Sláine, dies in penitence.

Fínnechta son of Lachtna, superior of Ferna, dies.

Kalends of January
[...]

Cluain Moccu Nóis was plundered by the men of Mumu.

U959.4 Jump to heading ¶

Maenach son of Cormac, superior of Les Mór, died.

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 959 alias 960.

Domnall son of Muirchertach led an army to Dál Araidi and took pledges.

Camán son of Amlaíb son of Gothfrith was defeated at Dub.

Muiredach son of Fergus made a great circuit of Connacht.

(Cathmug, superior of Les Mór, rested.)

Kalends of January
[...]

An arrow-like flash of lightning came right through Laigin from the south-west and killed eleven hundred men and animals as far as Áth Cliath.

Erchad's son, king of Uí Briúin Sheóla, died.

Ualgarc, king of Dartraige, was killed by his own people.

(Fer Gráid, king of Caisel, was killed by his own people.)

U961.5 Jump to heading ¶

Conaing ua Domnalláin, superior of Clochar of the Sons of Daiméne, rested.

U962.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 961 alias 962.

Eógan son of Muiredach, tributary king of Ireland, was killed by the Uí Fhailgi.

U962.3 Jump to heading ¶

Aengus ua Maíl Doraid was killed by his own people.

Kalends of January
[...]

Mael Muire son of Eochaid, successor of Patrick, was bone.

U963.4 Jump to heading ¶

Cellachán's son, king of Caisel, dies.

Gothfrith son of Amlaíb died.

U963.6 Jump to heading ¶

The successor of Tigernach, i.e. Caenchomrac, dies.

U963.7 Jump to heading ¶

(Ualgarc ua Maíl Trea was killed by the Mugdorna Maigen.)

U964.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 963 alias 964.

The above year was the last of the complete Paschal Cycle from the arrival of Patrick in Ireland.

U964.2 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Ruanaid son of Flann son of Éicnechán, and his son, were killed by the sept of Fiangus.

Dub Scúile son of Cinaed, successor of Colum Cille, rested.

Cell Dara was plundered by the foreigners, but was compassionated with a wonderful kindness through Niall ua Eruilb, almost all the clerics being ransomed for the honour of God: with his own silver Niall ransomed of them as many as would fill Brigit's great house and the oratory.

U965.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 964 alias 965.

Great and intolerable famine in Ireland, so that the father was wont to sell his son and daughter for food.

The Uí Chanannáin inflicted a battle-rout, and Domnall fell therein.

A change of abbots at Ard Macha, i.e. Dub dá Leithe instead of Muiredach from Sliab Cuilinn.

U965.6 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall ua Néill, king of Temair, made an expedition and plundered Connacht, taking hostages from ua Ruairc.

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 965 alias 966.

Mael Muire, daughter of Niall son of Aed, died.

U966.3 Jump to heading ¶

Dub dá Bairenn, successor of Buite, ended his life.

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 966 alias 967.

Dub son of Mael Coluim, king of Scotland, was killed by the Scots themselves.

Aed ua hAitid, king of Uí Echach, was killed by his own people.

Mathgamain son of Cennáitig, king of Caisel, plundered and burned Luimnech.

U968.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 967 alias 968.

Cellach ua Banan, successor of Comgall, dies.

Muiredach, successor of Cainnech, and Flaithbertach son of Muiredach, king of Uí Echach, die.

U968.3 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall ua Néill led an army to Laigin and plundered them from Berba westwards to the sea, taking a great spoil in cows, and he beleaguered the foreigners and the Laigin for two months.

Connmach, successor of Ultán, rested.

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 968 alias 969.

U969.1 Jump to heading ¶

Cinaed ua Cathmaíl, superior of Daire Calgaig, Mael Finnéin son of Uchtán, bishop of Cenannas and successor of Ultán and Cairnech, and Eógan son of Cleirech, bishop of Connacht, rested.

U969.2 Jump to heading ¶

Saerlaith, daughter of Elcomach, died aged one hundred.

U969.3 Jump to heading ¶

Beollán son of Ciarmac, king of Loch Gabor, rested in Christ.

U970.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 969 alias 970.

U970.1 Jump to heading ¶

Cenannas was plundered by Amlaíb Cuarán.

U970.2 Jump to heading ¶

Ualgarc ua Ruairc was defeated and killed with very many others by Conchobor son of Tadc.

U970.3 Jump to heading ¶

The king of Ulaid, i.e. Ardgar son of Matudán, made an expedition with the foreigners and sacked Connaire, leaving a great many beheaded there.

U970.4 Jump to heading ¶

The battle of Cell Móna was won by Domnall son of Congalach and Amlaíb against Domnall ua Néill, and there fell there Ardgar son of Matudán, king of Ulaid, and Donnacán son of Mael Muire king of Airgialla, and Cinaed son of Cróngall, king of Conaille, and very many others.

U970.5 Jump to heading ¶

The sacking of Lugbad and Druim Inasclainn by Murchad, king of Ailech.

U970.6 Jump to heading ¶

The sacking of Mainister and Lann Léire by Domnall, king of Ireland, in which three hundred and fifty were burned in one house.

U971.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 970 alias 971.

U971.1 Jump to heading ¶

Cuilén son of Illulb, king of Scotland, was killed by the Welsh in a battle-rout.

U971.2 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall ua Néill, king of Temair, was driven from Mide by the Clann Cholmáin.

U971.3 Jump to heading ¶

Niall son of Aed, king of Ulaid, dies.

U971.4 Jump to heading ¶

Tuathal, successor of Ciarán, and Mael Samna, successor of Cainnech, die.

U971.5 Jump to heading ¶

Cellach ua Nuadat was killed by foreigners in front of the refectory.

U971.6 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall ua Néill led an army against the men of Mide, and plundered all their churches and forts, and plundered Uí Fhailgi and Fotharta.

p.411

U972.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 971 alias 972.

U972.1 Jump to heading ¶

A battle between the Ulaid and the Dál Araidi in which fell the king of the Province, i.e. Aed son of Loingsech, and others.

U972.2 Jump to heading ¶

Murchad son of Finn was deceitfully killed by Domnall Claen.

U972.3 Jump to heading ¶

Cathasach son of Fergusán, coarb of Dún, dies.

U972.4 Jump to heading ¶

Fogartach son of Niall ua Tolairg was treacherously killed by Domnall son of Congalach.

U972.5 Jump to heading ¶

Crunnmael, superior of Glenn dá Locha, dies.

U973.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 972 alias 973.

U973.1 Jump to heading ¶

Conchobor son of Tadc, king of Connacht, dies.

U973.2 Jump to heading ¶

A battle between Murchad ua Flaithbertaig and the Connachta, in which fell Cathal son of Tadc, king of Connacht, and Géibennach son of Aed, king of Uí Maini, and many others.

U973.3 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Muire, superior of Dairmag, was drowned in Es Ruaid.

U973.4 Jump to heading ¶

Bécán, successor of Finnén, and Ailill, superior of Glenn dá Locha, died untroubled deaths.

U973.5 Jump to heading ¶

Dub dá Leithe, successor of Patrick, made a visitation of Mumu and obtained his demand.

U974.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 973 alias 974.

U974.1 Jump to heading ¶

Murchad son of Flaithbertach went on a foray in Cenél Conaill and took a great spoil; and one dart struck him, and he died thereof at Dún Clóitige, with communion and penance.

U974.2 Jump to heading ¶

Diarmait son of Dochartach, successor of Mo-Laise, died.

U974.3 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad Finn, king of Mide, was killed by Agda son of Duibcenn.

U974.4 Jump to heading ¶

Úgaire son of Tuathal inflicted a rout on the Osraige in which Diarmait son of Donnchad fell. In a second battle the Osraige defeated the Uí Cheinnselaigh, and Domnall son of Cellach fell.

p.413

U975.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 974 alias 975.

U975.1 Jump to heading ¶

Edgar son of Edmund, king of the Saxons, rested in Christ.

U975.2 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall son of Eógan, king of the Britons, died on pilgrimage, and Fogartach, abbot of Daire, died.

U975.3 Jump to heading ¶

Ferdal, superior of Rechru, was killed by the heathens.

U975.4 Jump to heading ¶

Cinaed ua hArtacáin, i.e. of the race of Cernach Sotal, chief poet of Ireland, rested.

U975.6 Jump to heading ¶

Very bad weather in the above year.

U976.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 975 alias 976.

U976.1 Jump to heading ¶

Mathgamuin son of Cennétig, king of Caisel, was killed by Mael Muad son of Bran.

U976.2 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad son of Cellach, king of Osraige, and Domnall son of Congalach, king of Brega, died.

U976.3 Jump to heading ¶

Conaing ua Fínáin, successor of Mac Nise and Colmán of Ela, rested.

U976.4 Jump to heading ¶

Tadc son of Ruaidrí, king of Cianacht, was killed in Ulaid.

U976.5 Jump to heading ¶

Sétna ua Demáin, superior of Naendruim, was burned to death in his own house.

U977.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 976 alias 977.

U977.1 Jump to heading ¶

Muirchertach son of Domnall ua Néill, and Congalach son of Domnall, two heirs designate of Ireland, were killed by Amlaíb son of Sitriuc.

U977.2 Jump to heading ¶

(Flaithbertach son of Muirchertach was born this year.)

U977.3 Jump to heading ¶

Gilla Coluim ua Canannáin was killed by Domnall ua Néill.

U977.4 Jump to heading ¶

Amlaíb son of Ollulb, i.e. King of Scotland, was killed by Cinaed son of Domnall.

U977.5 Jump to heading ¶

Conaing son of Cadán, successor of Moedóc, died.

U978.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 977 alias 978.

U978.1 Jump to heading ¶

Fiachra, superior of Í, rested.

U978.2 Jump to heading ¶

A battle between Brian son of Cennétig and Mael Muad, king of Desmumu, in which Mael Muad fell.

U978.3 Jump to heading ¶

The battle of Bithlann was won over the Laigin by the foreigners of Áth Cliath, and in it fell the king of Laigin, i.e. Úgaire son of Tuathal, and many others.

p.415

U978.4 Jump to heading ¶

The Airgialla inflicted a battle-rout on the Cenél Conaill, in which Niall ua Canannáin and many others fell.

U978.5 Jump to heading ¶

Corcach Mór of Mumu was sacked by fire.

U978.6 Jump to heading ¶

Les Mór Mo-Chutu was plundered and burned.

U979.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 978 alias 979.

U979.1 Jump to heading ¶

Muirenn daughter of Congalach, successor of Brigit, rested.

U979.2 Jump to heading ¶

Lethlobar ua Fiachna, king of Dál Araidi, was deceitfully killed.

U979.3 Jump to heading ¶

Conchobor son of Finn, king of Uí Fhailgi, died.

U979.4 Jump to heading ¶

Airechtach ua Caráin, the head of Irish learning, rested in peace.

U980.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 979 alias 980.

U980.1 Jump to heading ¶

The battle of Temair was won by Mael Sechnaill son of Domnall against the foreigners of Áth Cliath and the Isles, and very great slaughter was inflicted on the foreigners therein, and foreign power ejected from Ireland as a result. There fell therein Ragnall son of Amlaíb, the son of the king of the foreigners, and Conamal, son of a tributary king of the foreigners, and many others.

U980.2 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall ua Néill, over-king of Ireland, died after penance in Ard Macha. (Maccán son of Scolaige, king of Delbna):

  1. The lad who today refuses me

The thirty loaves which I can see

Will be thankful to share them

At the close of Domnall's reign. 2. Would that we had not heard the report

That Temair's sovereign had been removed!

A scarcity of grain, abundance of grass

Violent nature will bring about.)

  1. (If the men of the world were not numerous

From Life to Letha,

Satiety from the hand of Domnall

Would cause them to be more plentiful.—Mac Coise sang this.)

p.417

U980.3 Jump to heading ¶

Mugrón, successor of Colum Cille in both Ireland and Scotland, ended a happy life.

  1. (Since the birth of God's Son from heaven

There are eight tens and nine hundred years

Till the death of Mugrón whom verses extolled,

The graceful successor of Colum.)

U980.4 Jump to heading ¶

Rumann ua hAedacáin, successor of Tigernach, and Murchad son of Riada, successor of Comán, rested.

U980.5 Jump to heading ¶

Dubgall son of Donnchad, heir designate of Ailech, was killed by his own kinsman, i.e. Muiredach son of Flann. Muiredach son of Flann was beheaded by his own sept before a full month had passed.

U980.6 Jump to heading ¶

Comaltán ua Cléirig, king of Uí Fhiachrach Aidni, dies.

U980.7 Jump to heading ¶

Tigernán ua Mael Doraidh, king of Cenél Conaill, was killed by his own people.

U980.8 Jump to heading ¶

Braen son of Murchad, king of Laigin, was taken prisoner by the foreigners and afterwards put to death.

U981.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 980 alias 981.

U981.1 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall ua hAitid, king of Uí Echach, and Loingsech son of Fogartach, king of Uí Nialláin, fell by one another.

U981.2 Jump to heading ¶

Cleirchéne son of Donngal, successor of Feichíne, Eógan ua Cadáin, successor of Brénainn, and Sínach son of Muirthilén, successor of Comgall, fell asleep in Christ.

U981.3 Jump to heading ¶

An abnormal mast-crop in the above year.

U982.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 981 alias 982.

U982.1 Jump to heading ¶

Bruatar son of Tigernach, king of Uí Cheinnselaig, dies.

U982.2 Jump to heading ¶

Árchú son of Niall was treacherously killed by the sons of Ardgar.

U982.3 Jump to heading ¶

Aed ua Dubdai, king of the north of Connacht, dies an untroubled death.

U982.4 Jump to heading ¶

The plundering of Cell Dara by Ímar of Port Láirge.

p.419

U983.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 982 alias 983.

U983.1 Jump to heading ¶

Cormac son of Mael Ciaráin, successor of Mo-Chutu, and Muiredach son of Muirecán, prior of Ard Macha, die.

U983.2 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Sechnaill, son of Domnall, and Glún Iairn, son of Amlaíb, inflicted a battle-rout on Domnall Claen, king of Laigin, and Ímar of Port Láirge, in which fell Gilla Pátraic son of Ímar and others—many being drowned or slain. (Gilla Pátraic son of Amlaíb).

U983.3 Jump to heading ¶

Aed ua Mothráin, successor of Da-Sinchell, was fatally wounded and died.

U984.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 983 alias 984.

U984.1 Jump to heading ¶

Uisíne ua Lapáin, superior of Daire Calgaig, and Muiredach ua Flannacáin, lector of Ard Macha, rest.

U984.2 Jump to heading ¶

Dub Darach son of Domnallán, king of Derlas, was killed by his own people.

U984.3 Jump to heading ¶

Domnall Claen, king of Laigin, was killed by the Uí Cheinnselaig.

U984.4 Jump to heading ¶

Flaithbertach ua hÁnluain, king of Uí Nialláin, was deceitfully killed by the Uí Bresail.

U985.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January fifth feria, fifth of the moon, AD 984 alias 985.

U985.1 Jump to heading ¶

Fogartach ua Congaile, superior of Daiminis, Flaithlem, superior of Saiger, Mael Finnia, superior of Domnach Patraic, rested in Christ.

U985.2 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Sechnaill son of Domnall had an army in Connacht, and he reduced Mag Aí to ashes. The Connacht made a covert(?) foray to Loch Aininn, and they burned the country and killed the king of Fir Chell. (Mael Sechnall son of Domnall ravaged Connacht, plundered its islands, and killed its chiefs.)

U986.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 985 alias 986.

U986.1 Jump to heading ¶

A great disturbance in Ard Macha on the Sunday 25 July before Lammas between the Uí Echach and the Uí Nialláin, and in it the son of Trénar son of Celecán and others fell.

U986.2 Jump to heading ¶

The Danes arrived on the coast of Dál Riata, that is, with three ships, and seven score of them were executed and others sold.

p.421

U986.3 Jump to heading ¶

Í of Colum Cille was plundered by the Danes on Christmas Night, and they killed the abbot and fifteen of the elders of the monastery.

U987.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 986 alias 987.

U987.1 Jump to heading ¶

The battle of Manu was won by Aralt's son and the Danes, and a thousand were slain therein.

U987.2 Jump to heading ¶

A great outbreak of St Vitus' Dance, and it caused death to a large number of people and cattle among the Saxons and Welsh and Irish.

U987.3 Jump to heading ¶

A great slaughter of the Danes who plundered Í, and three score and three hundred of them were slain.

U988.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January first feria, ninth of the moon. AD 987 alias 988.

U988.1 Jump to heading ¶

Dúnlang son of Dub dá Baireann, heir designate of Caisel, and Muirgius son of Conchobor fell by one another in Uí Briúin Shinna.

U988.2 Jump to heading ¶

Congalach ua Cuilennáin, king of Conaille, and Ciar Chaille son of Cairellán, king of northern Brega, fell by one another.

U988.3 Jump to heading ¶

Laidcnén son of Cerball, king of Fernmag, was killed in Ard Macha by Fergal son of Conaing, king of Ailech.

U988.4 Jump to heading ¶

Colum, superior of Corcach, and Dub dá Bairenn, superior of Both Chonais, fell asleep.

U988.5 Jump to heading ¶

(Or it is under thus year that Dúnchad ua Braín should be.)

U989.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 988 alias 989.

U989.1 Jump to heading ¶

Dúnchad ua Braín, successor of Ciarán, an excellent scribe and a most religious man, died on his pilgrimage in Ard Macha on the fourteenth of the Kalends of February 19 Jan..

U989.2 Jump to heading ¶

Dún Lethglaise was plundered by the foreigners and burned.

U989.3 Jump to heading ¶

Glún Iarn, king of the foreigners, was killed when drunk by his own slave.

U989.4 Jump to heading ¶

Gothfrith son of Aralt, king of Inse Gall, was killed in Dál Riata.

U989.5 Jump to heading ¶

Dúnchad ua Robocáin, successor of Colum Cille, died.

p.423

U989.6 Jump to heading ¶

Eochaid son of Ardgar, king of Ulaid, went on an expedition to Cenél Eógain, and left behind ua hAitid dead.

U989.7 Jump to heading ¶

Dub dá Leithe, successor of Patrick, took the successorship of Colum Cille by the counsel of the men of Ireland and Scotland.

U989.8 Jump to heading ¶

Echmílid son of Rónán, king of Int Airthir, was killed by the descendants of Conall the Craftsman.

U989.9 Jump to heading ¶

Mac Léiginn son of ua Murchudáin, superior of Cúl Rathain, dies.

U990.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 989 alias 990.

U990.1 Jump to heading ¶

Daire Calgaig was plundered by the Danes.

U990.2 Jump to heading ¶

Urard son of Cos, chief poet of Ireland, and Aed ua Maíl Doraid, i.e. king of Cenél Conaill, died.

U990.3 Jump to heading ¶

The battle of Cam Fordroma was won by Mael Sechnaill over Tuadmumu, and Domnall son of Lorcán, king of Uí Fharca, and many others fell therein.

U991.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 990 alias 991.

U991.1 Jump to heading ¶

Donnchad ua Congalaigh, heir designate of Temair, was deceitfully killed by Mael Sechnaill.

U991.2 Jump to heading ¶

There was killed Tadc son of Donnchad, heir designate of Osraige,—by the men of Mumu—, Aed ua Ruairc, heir designate of Connacht, and Dub Darach ua Fiachna—by the Cenél Eógain.

U992.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January
[...]
. AD 991 alias 992.

U992.1 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Petair ua Tolaig, successor of Brénainn, and Mael Finnia ua Maenaigh, successor of Ciarán of Cluain, fell asleep.

U992.2 Jump to heading ¶

Donn ua Duinn Chuan, king of Tethba, dies.

U992.3 Jump to heading ¶

An expedition was made by Mael Sechnaill in Connacht, and he brought away great spoils.

U992.4 Jump to heading ¶

A remarkable manifestation on St. Stephen's night, the sky appearing blood-red.

U993.0 Jump to heading ¶

Kalends of January first feria, fourth of the moon. AD 992 alias 993.

U993.1 Jump to heading ¶

Tuathal son of Ruba, successor of Finnén and Mo-Cholmóc, and Conchobor son of Cerball ua Maíl Shechnaill, died.

p.425

U993.2 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Ruanaid ua Ciarda, king of Cairpre, was killed by the men of Tethba.

U993.3 Jump to heading ¶

Two of the Uí Channanáin were killed.

U993.4 Jump to heading ¶

Éicnech ua Leocháin, king of Luigne, was killed by Mael Sechnaill in the abbot's house in Domnach Pátraic.

U993.5 Jump to heading ¶

Mael Finnia ua hAenaig, successor of Feichíne and bishop of the peoples of Luigne, rested in Jesus Christ.

U993.6 Jump to heading ¶

Cléirchéne son of Mael Dúin, king of Uí Echach, was killed by his own people.

U993.7 Jump to heading ¶

A great mortality of people, cattle, and bees throughout Ireland this year.

U993.8 Jump to heading ¶
